appearance.identity: Restored 1659 Maltese coastal watchtower with battered limestone plinth, two projecting stringcourses, elevated inland entry, seaward window, shallow roof embrasures and a corner stair shelter.
appearance.master: Preserve the current22250triangle detailed exterior and imported master bytes.
appearance.browser: All four levels retain the battered body, projecting stringcourses, raised inland door, opposite sea window, flank loop, open terrace/parapet notches, corner stair shelter and flagpole. Far arches aggregate their shallow curved heads; district uses coarse flat stone courses; street retains original course rhythms as flat cards; closeup retains the detailed master.

limitations: Current restored exterior is modeled. The internal rooms, spiral stair and neighboring World War II pillboxes are separate from this exterior asset.
Individual masonry joints and repair tints are original reconstructions of the photographic pattern; they are not a stone-by-stone survey.
Mapped plan is approximately 8.5 m square. No target-specific measured elevation was published in the consulted inventory; heights and small roof fittings are proportioned from primary photographs.

Current browser levels aggregate shallow distant arch heads and individual stone relief; no coastal rock/terrain survey, interior, individual conservation stone pattern or physical-device performance claim.
